title: A latent two-head bioelectric pattern is a counterfactual memory of the future target form

fields.label: Label
fields.value: A latent two-head bioelectric pattern is a counterfactual memory of the future target form

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because a two-headed bioelectric pattern can exist in an anatomically normal one-headed planarian with normal gene expression, the bioelectric pattern is not a readout of current anatomy but a representation of the target morphology to be built if the animal is injured, in effect a counterfactual memory.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Reprogrammability, external manipulation, and representation

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In the case of a two-headed pattern in a one-headed host, this means that the bioelectrical pattern is not a read-out of what the anatomy is currently, but rather a representation of what it should be, weeks later, following regeneration if the animal is injured.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind”, Animal cognition (2023), doi:10.1007/s10071-023-01780-3; section “Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Reprogrammability, external manipulation, and representation”. Scope: Planarian flatworms with altered bioelectric patterns (Durant et al. 2017)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-glue-13: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.51

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Prospective prediction of later morphology from a latent voltage pattern is empirically testable and informative. The semantic upgrade from predictive state to counterfactual memory is not uniquely distinguished from a causal physiological precursor.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In anatomically one-headed worms, test whether a pre-injury voltage pattern predicts two-headed regeneration better than current anatomy and gene expression, using blinded prospective outcomes. Prediction supports latent state information, while 'representation' and 'counterfactual memory' require an additional theory-dependent criterion.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Matched pre-injury voltage and later outcome data may be limited.

Normal gene expression depends on assay resolution and timing.

A predictive biomarker need not be a representation.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.42
discriminating power: 0.42
analysis feasibility: 0.68
operationalizability: 0.55
data existence: 0.5

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The dissociation among current anatomy, voltage pattern, expression, and later head number is a real empirical test and is what the cited experiment reports. Those data are not an open, reanalyzable set. Calling the pattern a counterfactual memory does not add a measurement that a non-representational cause of the later anatomy would fail.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In anatomically one-headed planarians, compare the bioelectric pattern and gene-expression profile with later head number after an experimental cut. A two-headed voltage pattern before injury, with ordinary anatomy and ordinary expression, that predicts two heads after the cut, would support a pattern that is not a readout of current anatomy; a voltage pattern that matches current head number would refute that dissociation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Voltage images and expression comparisons are in the source paper's figures, not a public image and count matrix.

Predicting the regenerative outcome is expected of any causal prepattern, with or without memory of a counterfactual target.
